authorization.user_instruction: Set it up with its own budget and everything; run the SafeCEM study with the safety dial on TwoRoom, adding a hazard region like Push-T.

environment.base_env: swm/TwoRoom-v1 (stable_worldmodel 0.1.1), default geometry; the subclass only adds the goal frame (agent drawn at the target) to info, as Push-T does
environment.success_rule: simulator terminated flag (agent centre within 16 px of the target)
environment.violation_rule: agent centre inside any true hazard box in a saved simulator state

hazard.description: A horizontal band of two axis-aligned hazard boxes spanning the right room midway between the start and the target, invisible to the world model and physically traversable, with one 24 px gap that overlaps the straight route. Raising d narrows the gap and squeezes it off the route; at d = gap_width/2 it closes and no safe route exists.

A.name: engineering
A.jobs: per layout: unconstrained (penalty, lam 0) on all three seeds; on T2: safe d=0 and safe d=6 on seed 100
acceptance: every engineering episode returns a complete result with 1 to 50 saved states
safe d=0 and d=12 differ from the unconstrained run in at least one saved state
the exact check replays every executed step of every episode to within 0.01 px
the unconstrained planner enters a true hazard box on at least one seed for at least one layout, otherwise report nothing to avoid and still run B
measured seconds per episode and workers recorded before the B freeze

B.name: dial_sweep
B.order: randomized job order with schedule seed 2026102512

C.name: multiobjective_search
C.clearance_schedule: d(t) = clip(d0 + d1 * t, 0, 80) for t = 0 .. horizon-1, applied to the predicted block t+1

redesign.reason: LeWM TwoRoom's goal cost (latent distance to the goal frame) is informative only within about 30 px of the target and flat or non-monotone beyond (rank correlation 0.41 with true distance over the arena), while its predictor is accurate (block squared error 14 to 36 against a displacement scale of 384). The paper evaluates TwoRoom with goals 25 dataset steps ahead, a median 40 px (p90 66 px) by our measurement, and calls TwoRoom LeWM's weakest environment. The v1 target was 154 px away through the door and the planner wandered off on CPU. Closed-loop CPU checks of the unconstrained planner: 4/4 successes at 30 px, 4/8 at 45 px, 2/8 at 60 px; failures drift to the wall, the door or a corner.
redesign.changes: start and target 50 px apart in the right room away from the door; budget 50 steps and 10 CEM iterations as in the LeWM TwoRoom evaluation; replanning every block (closed loop) kept because open-loop execution failed more often on CPU. v3: the gap overlaps the straight route (offsets 0, 6, 12 px, width 24) and the band spans the room, because in a v2 CPU pilot with gaps 13 and 25 px off the route the constrained planner failed 0/8 (it lost the goal signal and drifted toward the door) while the unconstrained planner reached the target 4/4 through the band.
redesign.v3_pilot: CPU, seed 21, first replan traced per CEM iteration: with LeWM's 300 samples and top 30, the constrained ranking removes the few candidates that reach the goal basin (the best feasible goal cost is 296 at d=4 against 60 overall), the elite mean drifts to a far-field minimum near the door and the episode fails, even with the gap on the route; 1000 samples with top 30 or 100 fail the same way. 1000 samples with top 10 (1%) converge to a feasible plan ending at the goal (cost 8) at d=4 on T0 and on T2. The planner therefore uses 1000 samples and top 10 in every condition, free and safe alike.
